title: Deep Utopia
subtitle: Life and Meaning in a Solved World
pitch: Superintelligence was about what could go wrong. This is about what happens if it goes right: when machines can do everything, what is left for us to do and why?
toc_note: The book is a week of lectures. Each day has many short sections. The guide below covers the days.

chapters.g: Bostrom explains the unusual format: a fictional week of lectures by an older Bostrom, with students, a fox named Feodor, and interruptions.
Economics of a solved world: Keynes's prediction of shorter working weeks, why our wants keep growing, and what full automation would really change.
Technological maturity and our cosmic endowment: what would still be impossible or worth doing when almost anything can be done by machines.
Full unemployment and the purpose problem. Case studies of shopping, exercise, learning and parenting show what happens when effort is no longer needed.
Plasticity and autopotency: if we can change our own minds and feelings, would a perfect world be boring? A long look at interestingness.
Pleasure, fulfilment, richness and purpose. Includes a fable called The Exaltation of ThermoRex.
The last day: what makes a life meaningful, using Thaddeus Metz's account, whether meaning can survive in utopia, and a short closing set of scenes as the week ends.

ideas: If AI goes well, most human work becomes unnecessary.
The hard question then is meaning and purpose, not money.
We could reshape our own minds, which changes what 'boring' means.
Some values, like play and relationships, might survive a solved world.

args.a: A solved world could still hold deep value and meaning.
args.c: Critics find the playful format hard to follow and argue that focusing on utopia distracts from avoiding catastrophe first.

questions: If you never needed to work again, what would you do with your days?
Would you change your own feelings if you could?

o: As a week of fictional lectures
quiz.w: Each chapter is a day of the week.

o: Humans losing reasons to act when machines can do everything
quiz.w: It is the worry that a solved world removes our reasons for effort.
